# LLDP test fixtures

Each `*.hex` file is one complete Ethernet frame (destination MAC first),
written as whitespace-separated hex bytes. Lines starting with `#` are
comments. `test_lldp.c` loads them with `load_hex()`.

## Provenance

The five vendor fixtures are **synthetic**. No real captures were available
when the parser was written, so `gen_fixtures.py` builds each frame from a
raw TLV encoder, modelled on the TLV set that the vendor's LLDP agent is
known to emit:

| File           | Modelled on                                   | Notable content |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| `cisco.hex`    | Catalyst 2960X, IOS 15.2                      | ifname port ID, 802.3at power, two MED policies, Cisco OUI 00-01-42 TLV, >192-byte sys desc (exercises truncation) |
| `aruba.hex`    | Aruba 2930F, ArubaOS-Switch 16.10             | local port ID, IPv4 + IPv6 mgmt addr with OID, three VLAN names, max frame 9220 |
| `juniper.hex`  | EX2300-24P, Junos 20.4                        | ifIndex-style local port ID, Juniper OUI 00-90-69 TLV |
| `ubiquiti.hex` | UniFi USW-24-PoE 6.5                          | Power via MDI *without* the 802.3at extension, zero padding after End TLV |
| `lldpd.hex`    | lldpd 1.0.x on Debian 12 with `-M 3`          | MAC port ID, station-only caps, 802.3 link-agg and six MED inventory TLVs (decoded into `link_agg` / `inventory` since 2026-10-24) |
| `fortiswitch.hex` | **Real frame**, FortiSwitch-108F v7.4.9 port1 (captured with `GET /frame?lldp`; hostname and serial replaced) | ifname port ID, no PVID/MED, 802.3 link-agg, Fortinet OUI 08-5b-0e TLVs: hostname, serial (decoded), model/serial record (unknown) |
| `page_status.ndjson` | **Real `/status.json`** from the bench (FS switch on mgi6), edited | six snapshots for `test_page.py`: finished ping; the same with hostile strings (`<img onerror>`, `</div><script>`) in switch and DHCP fields; link down; a continuous ping with losses and a probe in flight; an 802.1X port with no DHCP and the blinker running; an AV network with an IGMPv3 querier and a PTPv2 grandmaster one hop away |

CDP fixtures (`cdp_*.hex`, 802.3/LLC/SNAP framing, generated by the same
script): `cdp_switch` (Catalyst 2960X, 16 TLVs incl. VoIP VLAN, VTP,
power available, odd-length checksum quirk), `cdp_phone` (IP phone with
power request), `cdp_router` (ISR with IP prefix and 4-byte MTU), `cdp_v1`
(CDPv1 from a 2950). Cross-checked with `scapy.contrib.cdp`.

Every generated frame is cross-checked with Scapy's LLDP dissector
(`scapy.contrib.lldp`) to make sure the encoding is well formed.

## Regenerating

```
python3 gen_fixtures.py          # rewrite the .hex files and dissect them
python3 gen_fixtures.py --check  # only dissect the existing files
```

Requires Python 3 and Scapy (`pip install scapy`) for the dissection check;
without Scapy the files are still written.

## Adding a real capture

Real frames are better than synthetic ones. To capture one:

```
sudo tcpdump -i en0 -s 0 -c 1 -w lldp.pcap 'ether proto 0x88cc'
python3 -c "
from scapy.all import rdpcap
f = bytes(rdpcap('lldp.pcap')[0])
print('\n'.join(' '.join(f'{b:02x}' for b in f[i:i+16]) for i in range(0, len(f), 16)))
" > vendor.hex
```

Or on Linux with lldpd running: `lldpcli show neighbors detail` confirms
what the switch is sending, and `tcpdump -xx` prints the raw bytes.

Then add a `test_<vendor>()` function in `test_lldp.c` with the expected
values, and register it in `TESTS[]` and `CMakeLists.txt`. Add the file name
to `FIXTURES[]` so the fuzz-style tests also mutate it.
